outcome: An effect that modifies how the activation cost may be paid applies to the total cost after increases and reductions, which the playability record's adjusted cost shows.
Only the object's controller (or owner if it has no controller) can activate its ability unless the object says otherwise, which the playability verdict shows.
Activating an ability puts it on the stack as a non-card object controlled by the activating player, and it later resolves, is countered or is moved.
Activating a cost-altering ability does not change the costs already paid for spells and abilities on the stack, which resolve as announced.
An ability that is prohibited from being activated is not offered as playable.
A creature's ability with {T} or {Q} in its cost is not playable unless the creature has been under its controller's control since the start of their most recent turn, or has haste.
A use restriction on an activated ability keeps applying after the object changes controller.
A use restriction on an acquired ability applies only to that ability as acquired from that object, not to identical abilities from other sources.
An 'Activate only as a sorcery' ability is playable only at sorcery timing: own main phase with an empty stack.
An 'Activate only as an instant' ability is playable whenever the player could cast an instant.
